breakfast.name: Poutine (Fries with Gravy)
breakfast.description: Canadian comfort food of crispy fries smothered in rich gravy and cheese curds
instructions: Fry potatoes in batches until golden
Drain on paper towels, season with salt
Make gravy: melt butter, whisk in flour
Add beef broth slowly while whisking
breakfast.notes: Gravy must be hot to slightly melt cheese curds
breakfast.fun_fact: Poutine originated in Quebec and is now a Canadian icon

lunch.name: Butter Tarts
lunch.description: Canadian sweet tarts with gooey butter filling and raisins
instructions: Line tartlet tins with pie crust
Filling should be bubbly but not overcooked
Cool slightly before removing from tins
lunch.notes: The gooey center is essential to authentic butter tarts
lunch.fun_fact: Butter tarts are a beloved Canadian dessert, often served at fairs and celebrations

dinner.name: Tourtière (Meat Pie)
dinner.description: Traditional French-Canadian meat pie with ground pork and spices
instructions: Brown pork with onion and garlic
Bake at 375°F for 45-50 minutes until golden
dinner.fun_fact: Tourtière is a French-Canadian Christmas tradition

snacks.name: Maple Taffy on Snow
snacks.description: Canadian maple candy made by pouring hot maple syrup on clean snow
instructions: Pack clean snow or shaved ice in pan or on clean surface
Slowly pour hot syrup in thin ribbons on snow
Let cool for 1-2 minutes until it sets
Roll each piece around popsicle stick
snacks.fun_fact: Maple Taffy on Snow is a popular treat at Canadian sugar shacks
alternatives: Use frozen beet juice for colored version

desserts.name: Beavertails (Fried Pastry)
desserts.description: Deep-fried pastry shaped like beaver tail, served with sweet toppings
instructions: Cut into oval beaver tail shapes
Fry until golden on both sides
Serve warm with chocolate or maple syrup
desserts.notes: Dough should be thin and crispy when fried
desserts.fun_fact: Beavertails are a Canadian pastry found at Canadian fairs and events

nonAlcoholicDrinks.name: Caesar Cocktail (Non-Alcoholic)
nonAlcoholicDrinks.description: Canadian drink with Clamato juice and spices, virgin version without alcohol
instructions: Add Clamato juice, Worcestershire, hot sauce
nonAlcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Caesars are so popular in Canada that some say more Caesars are consumed there than Bloody Marys in the US

alcoholicDrinks.name: Canadian Whisky
alcoholicDrinks.description: Light, smooth Canadian whisky often made from corn base, served on rocks or neat
alcoholicDrinks.notes: Lighter and smoother than American bourbon
alcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Canadian whisky is known for its smooth, accessible taste
